items.excerpt: Figma argues that AI accelerates execution but not clarity, so teams increasingly mistake polished AI output for a sound decision. It lays out the context layers — design systems, a stated point of view, explicit constraints — that keep fast AI work pointed at the right problem instead of generating tech debt.

A practical UX framework for deciding where an AI feature physically lives in a product — floating widget, inline assist, sidebar or a dedicated hub. The argument is that placement, not model quality, determines whether users discover, trust and keep using the AI.

The piece names the gap between what AI is actually reliable for and what it merely looks reliable for, and argues that most design-team AI enablement programs fail in exactly that gap. It pushes teams to define task-level reliability boundaries before rolling AI out across a craft workflow.

A rethink of how design leadership works when a team is part human, part agent swarm. It swaps the org-chart model for flocking behaviour — shared direction and local rules — as the way to coordinate designers running many AI agents at once.

"Everyone can design" is back as AI tools hand generation to non-designers — but this time, the author argues, designers hold the leverage. The essay reframes democratised tooling as permission for designers to ship without waiting on others.

Part three of zeroheight's AI-ethics series asks whether AI-augmented design systems really democratise design or just concentrate authorship in whoever writes the rules. It examines who gains access, who loses judgement, and what governance a system team owes its consumers.

A build log of Moodle's design system rebuilt from scratch to be consumed by machines, not just humans — structured tokens, documentation and component metadata that AI agents can read directly. It is a concrete template for making a design system agent-legible.

zeroheight details the Design System Documentation Spec now moving through the W3C, aiming to standardise how component docs are structured across tools. A shared machine-readable doc format is the missing half of design tokens for AI-driven handoff.

Google is adding a toggle that removes the visible sparkle watermark from images and video made with its Nano Banana, Omni and Lyria models, while invisible SynthID marks and C2PA metadata stay attached. It changes what AI-generated creative assets look like when they ship into client work.

Bakatako is a daily doodle site where artists draw and share one prompt a day with no feeds, metrics or generators. Creative Bloq frames it as a deliberate human-made counterweight to the AI-art flood — a signal about where illustrators are putting their attention.

Vercel's new @ai-sdk/harness-acp package is a meta adapter that lets any Agent Client Protocol-compatible harness run through the AI SDK's HarnessAgent. For product teams building AI features into interfaces, it removes the per-vendor rewrite when swapping agent runtimes.

Grok Build is now available in the AI SDK harness layer via the @ai-sdk/harness-grok-build adapter, built on the ACP harness. Prompt-to-UI builders can call it through the same HarnessAgent interface as every other coding agent.

A blunt audit of what AI logo generators actually hand over — raster files, no type licensing, no system — now that people are launching brands on them. Useful ammunition for designers arguing the gap between a mark and an identity system.

A build write-up of AgentForge, a visual node-based builder for custom AI agents with tool calling. The most requested feature turned out to be a UI one: live cards showing each tool call's inputs, outputs and timing — a concrete pattern for designing agent transparency.

Facebook has shipped a standalone Creator Studio app with an AI creator assistant that reads performance and audience data, surfaces the comments worth answering, and drafts replies in the creator's voice. It pushes AI from asset generation into the creator's day-to-day operating loop.

DeepSeek released an open-source coding harness positioned against Claude Code, alongside updated V4-Pro weights on its API. For design-engineering teams it widens the set of self-hostable agents that can turn specs and mockups into working front-end code.

Google's Gemini 3.7 Flash is aimed squarely at coding and agent workloads with a 50% introductory price cut. Cheaper fast-tier models are what make always-on design-to-code and UI-critique agents affordable to run in a product team's loop.
